summary:
The Earth System Trends Detective project consists of developing a technological solution focused on analyzing, identifying, and interpreting trends in the planet's environmental variables, using scientific data provided by NASA. The tool aims to transform large volumes of environmental information into understandable indicators, allowing users to visualize and investigate changes occurring in different components of the Earth System.

This innovation addresses a fundamental challenge in environmental science: the difficulty of identifying, interpreting, and understanding trends in large scientific datasets. Although various variables, such as temperature, precipitation, soil moisture, and aerosol concentration, are continuously monitored, their behaviors can present significant differences depending on the region and the period analyzed. This makes it difficult to identify patterns and understand environmental transformations on a global and regional scale.

To solve this problem, the project proposes an investigative approach based on data analysis, identifying increasing and decreasing trends, as well as possible changes in environmental patterns. In this way, the system allows users to investigate different variables, understand their behavior over time, and identify signs of changes in how the planet functions.
details:
Sherlock Terra: Detective of Earth System Trends

Uncovering Earth's Trends.

About the Project

Sherlock Terra is a project developed as part of the NASA Space Apps Challenge, with the goal of making Earth observation data more accessible and facilitating the investigation of environmental trends.

The proposal is to provide a tool that allows users to explore climate data, identify patterns over time, and compare the behavior of different regions across the planet.

In its current version, developed as a Minimum Viable Product (MVP) prototype, the project works with approximately 45 years of historical data (1981–2025), combining precipitation and temperature information from nine regions across South America, Oceania, and Europe.

The focus of this version is to investigate how these regions behave during El Niño, La Niña, and neutral conditions.

The system presents data, trends, and statistical results to support the investigation. The interpretation of the results is left to the analyst.

Features

Regional Comparison

Users can select two regions through dropdown menus and define the range of years they wish to investigate.

The data is displayed side by side, allowing users to compare the climate behavior of each location and observe potential differences and similarities.

Precipitation and Temperature Charts

The dashboard displays historical precipitation and temperature time series, highlighting El Niño and La Niña periods along with their respective trend lines.

Users can choose which variables to display and switch between two visualization modes:

  • Observed Values: Displays the recorded values for each region.
  • Anomalies Relative to the Trend: Shows how values have behaved in relation to the long-term trend, making it easier to compare regions with different rainfall levels and climate characteristics.

The interactive legend allows users to show or hide chart elements according to their analytical needs.

Regional Map

The dashboard features a map displaying the geographical distribution of the regions included in the project.

This visualization allows users to identify the locations of the analysis points and better understand the spatial distribution of the regions used in the comparisons.

Pacific Ocean Phenomenon Index

The dashboard displays the Oceanic Niño Index (ONI), provided by NOAA, as a quarterly time series.

This indicator allows users to track ENSO phases and cross-reference them with climate conditions observed in the selected regions.

É um componente importante do orçamento de energia de superfície da Terra. O fluxo de calor latente é comumente medido com a técnica da razão de Bowen ou por covariância turbulenta. projectRefs: A RADARSAT Constellation Mission (RCM) é a nova geração de satélites de observação da Terra do Canadá. O RCM inclui um trio de satélites de observação da Terra, capazes de escanear a Terra dia ou noite e em quaisquer condições climáticas. A configuração de três satélites permite revisitas diárias do vasto território e abordagens marítimas do Canadá, bem como acesso diário a 90% da superfície mundial e ao Ártico até quatro vezes por dia. Mais de uma dúzia de departamentos do governo federal já utilizam dados do RADARSAT para prestar serviços importantes aos canadenses.
